writtenBefore: any 2024 data was fetched or looked at; committed before the fetch so git history shows the order
question: Do the loss-scale and early-season win-scale changes found by exploring 2025 hold up on a season none of them was tuned on?
why: Experiment 1 selected only unrankedLossPenalty=4. Exploring 2025 afterwards (post-hoc, so not evidence) suggested every loss is under-punished 2-3x and early-season wins are under-moved. Every value below was fit on 2025; 2024 only confirms or rejects.

holdout.construction: identical to experiment-1's tuning data: scripts/fetch-pickem-history.mjs (CFBD /rankings, /games, /lines, regular season), scripts/lib/pickem-history.mjs (same Elo stand-ins, provider order, quality-win rule, and alignment check)

check.transitions: poll weeks 1-3 (weeks 1-2 rebuilt from git, week 3 live snapshot), each against the next AP poll

context.use: where the values were fit; reported for reference, not evidence

metric: weighted pairwise order errors, exactly as experiment-1 (transitions out of poll weeks 1-2 weigh 0.5, later 1.0; exits tied just below #25; entrants not scored)

LS.source: 2025, one-standard-error rule (experiment-1 R5) over lossScale [1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4]; best 3, reported 2.5

LSW.source: 2025, same rule over earlyWinScale [1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3] on top of LS; best and reported 1.25; the week-8 boundary comes from experiment-1's early (3-8) / late (9+) split

chain.asks: does experiment-1's pick beat V1 on a new season?
does loss scaling beat whatever step 1 left in place?
does the early-season win scale add to loss scaling?

chain.label: penalty 4
chain.asks: does the unranked-loss penalty still add anything on top? (2025 said no)

passRule: a step's candidate replaces the current model only if, on 2024: weighted errors fall (delta > 0); the 5th percentile of the summed improvement over 10,000 bootstrap resamples of 2024 transitions (seed 20260923) is > 0; neither half of the season (poll weeks 1-8, 9+) gets worse; and the improvement stays > 0 after removing every pair involving any single team
checkGuard: the final model's weighted errors on 2026 weeks 1-3 must not exceed V1's; if they do, fall back through the adopted models to the last one that passes
outcome: the chain's final model is the recommendation; every model's numbers on 2024, 2026 and 2025 are reported either way
